scope: Proposition 5.7 (Naming bounded data) of the manuscript “Eventual categoricity for abstract elementary classes” (preprints/Eventual-Categoricity-for-Abstract-Elementary-Classes-September-24-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 240 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 dcb7401285f5ac78), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 34. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let C be a working scheme, and fix a bounded list c and its diagram, witnessed at some eligible level. After increasing the fixed lower threshold, the objects with a named realization of this diagram, and arrows preserving the names, form a working scheme. This includes naming enumerations of fixed small strong models in the vertices, with their specified maps. The additional lower bound can be chosen in terms of the original scheme and the cardinality of the named list, independently of the level at which that list was first witnessed.
